components.name: Accordion
components.description: An `Accordion` allows users to toggle the display of sections of content.
components.usage:
Groups related content and lets users collapse/expand it under a section title, so they can scan titles and decide where to look.

**Rules**
- Use for large amounts of groupable content (e.g. settings configurations).
- Do NOT use an accordion to hide important inputs or controls required for the current task.
- Secondary title and leading icon are optional (off by default).

components.name: AudioPlayerControls
components.description: Presentational, fully controlled audio controls (play/pause, seek, elapsed time, playback speed and optional download). It owns no `<audio>` element and no playback state, so it can be driven by any source — a local element or a shared/persistent one. `AudioPlayer` wraps this with its own element for the common self-contained case.

components.name: AutoComplete
components.description: An input for selection of options.

props.name: renderSelected
props.type: ComponentType<{ selected: AutoCompleteOption<TLabel>; onRemove?: (event: MouseEvent<HTMLButtonElement>) => void; }>

props.name: renderItem
props.type: ComponentType<{ role?: string; label: TLabel; value: string; selected?: boolean; focus?: boolean; onMouseDown: MouseEventHandler; }>

components.name: Avatar
components.usage:
A visual, thumbnail representation of a single user or entity.

**Rules**
- Represents a SINGLE user or entity (not groups).
- Always provide meaningful alt text for images — critical for screen readers.
- Choose the size to match the surrounding context.
- Use the letter (initials) fallback when no image is available.

components.name: Badge
components.description: Communicates notification’s amount and types.
components.usage:
Indicates the type and quantity of notifications, highlighting key events and facilitating user navigation.

**Rules**
- Pick `variant` by the EVENT semantics it represents (e.g. `primary` for a thread reply, `danger` for a user mention), not by color preference — the options are named by color, but each maps to a specific semantic meaning.
- Never exceed 3 characters; show "99+" for anything above 99.
- Use the small dot variant (empty content) when you only need to signal that something new exists, or when the quantity can't be shown.

components.name: Banner
components.usage:
A system-level, non-time-based notification fixed at the top of the viewport. Communicates that something happened or is about to happen. Dismissibility depends on the notification's importance.

**Rules**
- Use for a whole-window/system condition (e.g. reconnecting, recording consent, blocked permissions) — for inline status tied to specific content use a Callout instead, and for brief action feedback use a Toast.
- Icon and title are mandatory; description is optional.
- Only show the "X of Y notifications" counter and prev/next controls when more than one banner is queued.
- A banner has no action-button slot — if the notification needs a decision, use a Callout instead.

components.name: Box

props.name: is
props.description: The `is` prop is used to render the Box as a different HTML tag. It can also be used to render a different fuselage component.

extends: Omit< SVGAttributes<SVGElement>, keyof AllHTMLAttributes<HTMLElement> | 'elevation' | keyof StylingProps >

components.name: Bubble
components.usage:
Floating control used in a scrollable feed or dynamic menu without pagination.

**Rules**
- Use in scrollable feeds or dynamic menus without pagination.
- Position: 8px below the top of the feed/menu, 8px above the bottom, 8px between two bubbles in the same space.

components.name: Button
components.description: Indicates an actionable user action.
components.usage:
Triggers events and actions. Use for actions that change data or how it is displayed, change a state, trigger an action, or navigate the user within the app or to a different site. Buttons can also link to external URLs.

**Rules**
- When more than one button is side by side, always wrap them in a Button group with an 8px gap; a lone button needs no group.
- In a button group, use Primary when the next step is evident, and Secondary when it is unclear; exactly one Primary per group, the rest Secondary.
- For destructive flows, initiate with a Secondary danger button, then confirm with a Primary danger button.
- Never rely on color alone to signal danger — keep a clear label (and icon if used).
- Set a leading icon only when the label needs visual support; skip it when redundant.
- Do not pair a regular Button with an Icon button — use Icon Only on a regular Button instead if a label-less button is needed beside text buttons.
- Loading: replace the icon with a spinner, disable the button, and keep the label copy unchanged.
- Labels: sentence case, no title case, no exclamation marks; avoid vague stand-alone verbs (e.g. "Create channel", not "Create").
- For lightweight in-text navigation, use a link instead of a Button.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.description: A container for grouping buttons that semantically share a common action context.
components.usage:
A container for grouping buttons that semantically share a common action context. By default the buttons are laid out with an 8px gap (4px with `small`, 16px with `large`).

**Joined**

The `joined` variant fuses the buttons into a single segmented control: no gap between segments, group-level rounded corners, and no dividers — buttons sit flush. `joined` takes precedence over the `small`/`large` spacing modifiers; it composes with `vertical`, `stretch`, and `align`.

The joined group carries a translucent background (the secondary button background at 60% opacity). With opaque buttons it is fully covered; it only shows through the **ghost** segment — picked by the group via `ghostPosition='start' | 'end'`, which turns the first or last segment transparent so the surface behind the group shines through. Use the ghost segment for auxiliary edge actions, e.g. the expand chevron of a split button or floating controls over media/video. It keeps hover/active/focus feedback, and by design it is always an edge segment — a middle button cannot be ghosted.

**Rules**
- Use 2–4 buttons in a joined group, with at most one Primary.
- Joined groups work with regular labeled Buttons, icon-only `square` Buttons, and IconButtons.
- Do not pair a regular Button with an IconButton — beside labeled buttons use an icon-only `square` Button; reserve IconButtons for groups made only of IconButtons.
- Keep a joined group homogeneous: every button in it must use the same size. Any Button size works, but never mix sizes inside the same joined group — the segments would no longer sit flush.

components.name: Callout
components.description: The `Callout` is used to get the user's attention explaining something important in the content of the current page.
components.usage:
A non-time-based notification (system- or user-level) that cannot be dismissed by the user and persists until its status changes. May contain links.

**Rules**
- Cannot be dismissed by the user — use only for status that persists until it changes.
- Description is mandatory; icon and title are optional.
- Make copy concise while explicitly naming the event and the affected object.
- A Callout CAN carry action buttons — use it (not a Banner) when the notification needs a decision.

components.name: Card
components.usage:
Displays content in a visually appealing manner.

**Rules**
- Vertical card — use Regular as the default; use Hero for priority info at the top of a page.
- Horizontal card — use within a list, among other list items; do NOT use as a stand-alone element.
- Use the Header/Content sections to compose the card body from other design-system components.

components.name: CardGroup
components.usage:
Arranges Cards together with consistent spacing.

**Rules**
- Vertical card groups use an 8px gap between cards; horizontal card groups use a 16px gap.

components.name: CheckBox
components.usage:
Allows users to select one or more options from a list. Unlike radio buttons and switches, it also supports an indeterminate state for groups with partial selection.

**Rules**
- Use a checkbox when more than one option can be selected, or for a single opt-in such as accepting terms of service.
- Use the indeterminate state only for a parent controlling a group with partial selection.

components.name: Chip
components.usage:
Used to communicate and manage input-field selections.

**Rules**
- Text is mandatory.
- A chip may have either a leading icon or a leading avatar — not both.
- Keep the close button when the chip represents a removable selection.

components.name: CodeSnippet
components.description: The `CodeSnippet` is used to show code or commands and make easier to copy them. The default button text is `Copy` but you can use the `buttonText` prop to handle translations in your project. Please check the `useClipBoard` hook in `fuselage-hooks` package, to handle the copy behaviour.
components.usage:
A specific code style developed for easy copy and sharing.

**Rules**
- Use when the platform needs to make server settings available to users in code form (easy copy/paste).
- Note: the design system also documents an interactive "Code block" variant (with a reload button and expand/collapse controls) — this component currently only implements static display + a copy button, not those interactive features.

components.name: Contextualbar
components.description: The `Contextualbar` has the purpose to persist and input information about the scope of the related page.
components.usage:
A persistent UI element showing relevant information and actions for the current page context, letting users input data and act without the page disappearing.

**Rules**
- Title is mandatory.
- Provide a mandatory empty state on both navigation levels.
- Never disable the confirmation button — allow submit, then show required-field errors after confirm.
- Prefer the contextual bar over a Modal for non-disruptive contextual input.

components.name: Divider
components.usage:
Separates sections of content.

**Rules**
- Use inset to separate related content within a wrapper.
- For a full-width stroke (e.g. separating a header from page content), use a border, not a divider.
- Vertical dividers are used between things like a menu and composer; horizontal + text is used e.g. on a login page.

components.name: EmailInput
components.description: An input for email addresses.

components.name: Field
components.description: A `Field` is a wrapper representing an entry in a form.
components.usage:
Wraps an input with the supporting copy elements (label, description, hint, link, error) and keeps that copy clear, concise and consistent.

**Rules**
- Label — accurately describe the information needed; mark required fields with an asterisk.
- Description — context/instructions that clarify the label; keep it clear and simple.
- Placeholder — only when an extra hint helps the user, since it disappears on input; don't repeat the label in the placeholder.
- Error message — explain the problem and give an actionable fix (e.g. "Invalid email address"); avoid vague or apologetic copy.
- Hint — explain technical terms or behaviors.
- There is no dedicated Select/Dropdown component — a select is composed from a text Field whose input shows a chevron-down as its trailing icon.

components.name: FieldGroup
components.description: A container for grouping fields that semantically share a common data context.

components.name: FramedIcon
components.usage:
Draws attention to a specific UI element with an icon inside a rectangular frame; communicates system state.

**Rules**
- Always use alongside text, never standalone.
- Not for user actions — use the Icon button for actions.
- Do not mix multiple color types in the same context.

components.name: IconButton
components.usage:
A label-less, icon-only button. More minimalistic than a regular button with text.

**Rules**
- Use only when a clear, recognizable icon represents the action and no text label is needed.
- When the button indicates a status (not just triggers it), use the icon that reflects the current status (e.g. bell = following, bell-off = not following).
- When paired with a Badge, don't combine mini/tiny icon buttons with large/medium badges.

components.name: InputBox
components.description: A decorated input control with support for addons. Usually you'll perfer to use `-Input` (e.g. <LinkTo kind='Forms/TextInput' story='Default'>`TextInput`</LinkTo>) components over this one because it works as a construction block for them.

components.name: Label
components.description: A caption for an input component.
components.usage:
The label for an input — names the field and marks whether it's required.

**Rules**
- May be used standalone, e.g. to label a Checkbox, Radio button or Toggle switch.
- Accurately describe the information needed; mark required fields with the required indicator.
- Avoid generic labels or unnecessary ownership wording.
- Use the info icon only when the field needs a tooltip explanation.

components.name: Margins
components.description: Add margins to the wrapped component.
components.usage: Add margins to the wrapped component.

components.name: Menu
components.usage:
Presents the actions a user can take at a given moment — selection or specific functionality.

**Rules**
- The item label is mandatory; the trailing element is optional (radio, checkbox, etc.).
- Use title/divider items to structure groups; mark destructive items as danger; disable items that are unavailable.
- A device picker / list of selectable options is a Menu with title groups + radio trailing elements — not hand-built rows.
- Position 4px from the trigger edge on the opening side; align the menu border to the trigger border.

props.name: is
props.description: A component that renders an IconButton

props.name: children
props.description: The trigger item followed by the submenu items. The **first** child is rendered as the entry in the parent menu — it may use the rich `MenuItem*` sub-components (`MenuItemIcon`, `MenuItemContent`, …). The **remaining** children populate the submenu that opens beside it.

components.name: MessageDivider
components.usage:
Separates message sections, appearing above them.

**Rules**
- Use the date to mark when messages were sent; use the unread indicator to highlight new messages.
- Omit the divider line itself for longer messages likely to wrap multiple lines.

components.name: Modal
components.usage:
A powerful component that temporarily blocks interaction with the main view to capture and hold the user's undivided attention with a distinct prompt or information window.

**Rules**
- Use for critical information, gathering input when a contextual bar isn't applicable, confirmations/decisions, or interruptive workflows.
- For low-priority information use a Toast instead; for non-disruptive contextual input prefer the Contextual bar.
- Title must use sentence case and contain no question mark; keep titles concise.
- Default the header to title only — hide any icon/thumbnail unless the modal is triggered by a Rocket.Chat app or the title strongly needs visual reinforcement.
- Never disable the confirmation (Primary) button — allow submit, then show required-field errors after the user clicks confirm.
- Footer actions use the Button component — typically one Primary (confirm) + one Secondary (cancel); for destructive confirmations the Primary becomes a danger button.

components.name: Pagination
components.usage:
Splits data into several pages, with navigation control and items-per-page. Usually used with tables.

**Rules**
- Use with paginated data sets, typically below a table.

components.name: PaletteStyleTag
components.description: Style tag to handle the theme of the application. Import `PaletteStyleTag` and use it on the application informing the desired theme. Toggle the theme on Storybook's Control panel to see the color changes.

components.name: ProgressBar
components.description: The `ProgressBar` is used to inform the user the progress of an operation.
components.usage:
Concisely presents consumption or progress statistics.

**Rules**
- Use the `variant` (info/success/warning/danger) to convey state according to consumption or progress.
- Note: the design system also documents a "+ info" variant (adding a label + counter) — this component does not implement that variant yet.

components.name: RadioButton
components.usage:
Allows users to select only one option from a set of mutually exclusive options.

**Rules**
- Use only for a single choice from a small set of mutually exclusive options.
- Avoid when the number of choices is large — consider another control.
- Do not add links to the radio label.
- Do not use for accepting terms of service or similar — use a checkbox instead.

components.name: Scrollable
components.description: Add scroll capability to the wrapped component.
extends: PropsWithChildren<{ horizontal?: boolean; vertical?: boolean; smooth?: boolean; onScrollContent?: (touching: { top: boolean }) => void; }>

components.name: SearchInput
components.description: An input for search queries.

components.name: Select
components.description: An input for selection of options.

components.name: Sidebar
components.usage:
The room-list sidebar — rows for rooms (channels/teams/discussions/DMs) grouped into collapsible categories.

**Rules**
- Build a room list from sidebar items grouped under collapsible categories.
- Use the unread status to highlight rooms with new activity; use badges for counts.

components.name: SidebarItem
components.usage:
A single room row within the chat sidebar.

**Rules**
- Use the unread status to highlight rooms with new activity; use badges for counts.
- Shows the room name, an optional avatar/icon, and a trailing timestamp/status.

components.name: Skeleton
components.usage:
A visual loading indicator, used to indicate in-progress loading.

**Rules**
- Pair the skeleton with the content that is about to appear, matching its shape.

components.name: Slider
extends: T extends number ? SliderProps<number> : SliderProps<[min: number, max: number]>

components.name: States
components.usage:
Appears when there is no data to display and, if possible, describes what the user can do next.

**Rules**
- The message should be neutral and helpful, accurately describing the state and suggesting next steps.
- Prefer a link over a primary button/CTA for the default empty state.
- The magnifying-glass icon is reserved for search-related empty states; otherwise the icon should reflect the context.

components.name: StatusBullet
components.description: The `StatusBullet` is used to inform the user status.
components.usage:
A round icon that shows a user's status, using both color and a smaller icon.

**Rules**
- Use accompanied by the user's name in proper context, or when the user is setting their own status.
- Each status color is paired with a smaller icon for accessibility — color is never the only channel.

components.name: StylingBox
components.description: Merges its `StylingProps` props into a `className` prop passed to a child element. This is intended to be used as a wrapper for components that accept styling props but don't need the weight of the `Box` component prop handling internally.

components.name: Table
components.usage:
Displays tabular data with sortable columns, selectable rows, and cell content (title/subtitle, tags, actions).

**Rules**
- Match the header column count to the row's column count.
- Supports multi-row selection (e.g. "3 items selected") and row actions.
- Typically paired with Pagination.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Tabs is a component to navigate around the UI using buttons arranged together with the selected tab highlighted.
components.usage:
Lets users move back and forth between groups of related content.

**Rules**
- Use tabs to group related content; use a tab within the Tabs component, not standalone.
- Do NOT use tabs to navigate to other pages.
- The tab bar can scroll horizontally — use as many tabs as needed.
- Position tabs directly beneath the page header.

components.name: Tag
components.description: Used for mentions
components.usage:
A quickly recognizable component used to display set values.

**Rules**
- Use the Primary type sparingly — it draws the most attention.
- A leading icon helps recognition and lowers cognitive load — add only when it clarifies the tag.

components.name: TextAreaInput
components.description: An input for multi-line plain-text editing.

components.name: TextInput
components.description: An input for any kind of single-line text.
components.usage:
Lets users input one or multiple string values.

**Rules**
- Compose text inputs through the Field wrapper to get consistent label/description/hint/error/link.
- Follow the Field UX-writing rules for all copy (clear labels, actionable error messages, hints for technical terms).

components.name: Throbber
components.description: Indicates content that has not loaded yet.
components.usage:
A visual loading indicator (spinner), used to indicate in-progress loading.

**Rules**
- Use a spinner for brief, indeterminate waits.

components.name: ToastBar
components.description: Shows alerts in a toast component.
components.usage:
A user-level, time-based notification that communicates the status of a performed action. Can be dismissed and may contain links. Disappears after a minimum of 5 seconds.

**Rules**
- Use only for brief action feedback — never for a persistent condition or a decision.
- Keep copy concise.
- For success, be explicit about the action and avoid "successfully"/exclamation marks (e.g. "Link copied", not "Copied!").
- For errors, include how to resolve the issue in a second line.

components.name: ToggleSwitch
components.usage:
Lets users quickly switch between two mutually exclusive states with instant feedback.

**Rules**
- Use when there are exactly two choices, such as enabling/disabling a setting.
- The change applies immediately — do not use a toggle when you don't want the interface affected right away (use a checkbox with an explicit save action instead).

components.name: Tooltip
components.usage:
Shows additional, complementary information about an element on hover.

**Rules**
- Position 4px from the trigger edge on the opening side; center the tooltip on the trigger.
- Never put vital information only in a tooltip — it's complementary and hover-only (unavailable on touch).
- Good for ambiguous elements (number badges, mentions) and icon buttons.
- Keep copy concise; line breaks are allowed.
